//: Type checking only — nothing is emitted. Node runs the .ts files directly, so the compiler's job here is to catch what type stripping cannot: it erases types without checking them. erasableSyntaxOnly is the important line, because it rejects the constructs (enums, parameter properties, namespaces) that type stripping cannot handle and that would therefore fail at runtime rather than at build time.
///exclude: seller/cre/analyst-verdict is the CRE workflow. It compiles to WASM against a pinned @chainlink/cre-sdk in its own node_modules, and the SDK's export map only resolves under moduleResolution 'bundler' — under this file's 'nodenext' every SDK import fails, and its own package.json has no "type": "module", so verbatimModuleSyntax rejects the ES syntax too. It has its own tsconfig and is typechecked by `npm run typecheck:cre`. Everything else under seller/cre/ (verdict.ts, attestation.ts, evidence-server.ts, settle-cli.ts) is ordinary repo code and stays in here.
